question:
Table projection points to wrong database after renaming
When I change the database or table name for a ClickHouse source in direct-query mode and save, the reprojected table still queries the old database. The schema row saves correctly but the live query table is rebuilt against the previous location, so my HogQL queries return data from the wrong place until I manually refresh or re-sync.

Tables with database-prefixed names are silently skipped during sync setup
When a default database is configured for a data source, schema names that include a database prefix are not split into separate database and table components. Instead, the full prefixed name is treated as the table name, causing schema lookups to fail and those tables to be skipped during synchronization.

Placeholders in storage path prefix left unresolved for continuous exports
When a batch export is configured without an end time, placeholders in the storage path prefix are written literally into file paths instead of being resolved. The table name placeholder, for example, appears as raw text in the generated paths rather than the actual table name.

Date placeholders left unresolved in manifest path for unbounded exports
When configuring a batch export without an end bound, the manifest file path retains the original template placeholders instead of substituting actual date values. I expected all template variables in my key prefix to be filled in, even for exports without an end bound.

Disabling sharing does not revoke access
When I disable sharing on a dashboard, the share link still works after a page reload. I expected that toggling sharing off would immediately invalidate access, since the enabled flag should control whether a configuration is considered active.

Tables vanish from the catalog under heavy load
When processing many tables, some tables disappear entirely from the generated catalog even though most of their fields are valid. The issue appears intermittently after adding more tables or when the total number of fields grows large. I expected all serializable tables to appear in the catalog regardless of how many other tables were processed.

Duplicate virtual relations for the same table
When a table can be reached through multiple parent paths in the schema, the catalog output contains duplicate relation definitions for that same table. For example, if table B is reachable from both table A and table C, the catalog generates two separate relations for B instead of one. I expected each table to appear as a single relation regardless of how many paths lead to it.

Parent navigation breaks after crossing a join
When I run a query that goes back to a parent table after crossing a join, the system throws an error about having no parent to navigate to. The same navigation works fine when I don't cross any joins. I expected the system to track parent tables correctly regardless of joins.

Failed data deletion request marked as completed after retry
When a person or property deletion request fails mid-pipeline and I retry from the failed step, the request ends up in completed status even though the underlying deletion never actually succeeded. The failure hook correctly marks it as failed, but the finalization step then overwrites that to completed because it accepts the failed state as a valid input. I expect failed requests to stay failed so I can investigate before re-approving.

HogQL event removal fails with confusing permissions error
When I submit a HogQL-based event deletion request, it immediately fails with an error about "no creator whose query permissions can be enforced." The request was created without a user associated with it — there is no creator at all, not even one lacking permissions. The error message makes it sound like a permissions problem rather than missing data, so I have no idea what to fix. I need to know that the request needs a creator assigned before it can proceed.

HogQL event deletion request never completes
After a HogQL-based event deletion job finishes successfully, the request stays in queued status instead of being marked as completed. It sits there indefinitely even though the events have already been deleted. I expected the request to transition to completed once the job runs.

Fingerprint projection jumps unexpectedly with two items
When I select two fingerprints from an issue, they suddenly appear far apart on the projection chart, but with just one selected they sit at the center. Adding or removing a single fingerprint causes the positions of all others to shift dramatically instead of staying stable.

Fingerprint projection shows fewer results than expected after recent update
I opened an issue with about fifteen fingerprints in the projection view, but only eight showed up as dots on the chart. The other fingerprints that I know exist in the database simply disappeared from the visualization with no error message. This started happening after the embedding query runner was updated to parse rows more strictly.

Feature flags returned in unpredictable order
When I fetch all flags for a team, the returned list comes in a different order each time. I was trying to diff two flag configurations, but the changing order made it impossible to tell if anything actually changed.

Cohort dependency resolution returns incomplete results
When I retrieve all cohort dependencies for a feature flag, some cohorts are missing from the list. Cohorts that are transitively referenced through other cohorts don't appear in the output. I expected every cohort in the full dependency chain to be included.

Scoping API key to a non-existent organization gives misleading error
When I create a personal API key and include an organization ID that doesn't exist, the error says "You must be a member of all organizations that you are scoping the key to." This is confusing because I might actually be a member of a real organization but mistyped the ID. The system should distinguish between an invalid organization ID and a membership issue.

False 'not a member' error when scoping API key to team
When the same team is included twice in the scope list, creating or updating an API key fails with an error saying I'm not a member of that team, even though I am. The request should either deduplicate the teams or give a clearer error.

Activity logs sent to all organizations despite empty scope
When I create a personal API key without selecting any organizations to scope it to, activity logs are still being sent to all of my organizations. I expected that by not selecting any organizations, no activity logs would be generated for that key.

Evaluation results from decision models show no reasoning
When I run evaluations using a decision model, every result comes back with an empty reasoning field, even though the verdict or score is populated correctly. With regular LLM judge evaluations, I get a one-sentence explanation for each result. The decision model path skips this entirely, so I can't see why a pass/fail was given.

Evaluation results missing reasoning explanation
When reviewing LLM judge evaluations, every result shows an empty reasoning field even though the judge model generates an explanation during evaluation. I expected each evaluation to include the judge's explanation for why a verdict was reached, but the reasoning text is always blank.

Queries sometimes report a timeout error even though they finish quickly
I run a dashboard query that normally completes in under a second, but occasionally it fails with a generic timeout message. When it does fail, the query itself clearly finished — I can tell because the underlying data warehouse shows the query completed. The problem seems to happen right at the deadline boundary, where the system's cancellation mechanism kills the database cursor just as the query finishes, making it impossible to fetch the results. I expected queries that complete within the timeout window to always succeed.

Intermittent timeout on long queries that finish within the limit
When I run a raw SQL query that takes very close to the maximum allowed execution time, it sometimes fails with a timeout error even though the query completed successfully. This only happens for queries that take a long time, and it seems to occur right at the timeout boundary. The background timer that monitors the query appears to fire at the exact moment the query finishes, causing a false timeout. I expected queries that finish within the time limit to always succeed.

Valid SELECT queries rejected as non-read-only
Running a simple SELECT query against Trino returns the error "Raw Trino queries must be read-only SELECT statements." The read-only validation is too aggressive and rejects legitimate read-only queries because it compares token values against the string "SELECT" instead of checking token types.

Activity log shows fields as changed when nothing was actually modified

When I update a record, the activity log sometimes reports that certain fields have changed even though I didn't modify them. This happens consistently for specific fields on certain model types. I expected the audit trail to only list fields whose values actually changed between the before and after states.

Client identifier silently dropped from activity logs
Our integration sends a client identification header on every request, but the identifier never shows up in the activity log entries. The value is a simple string well within length limits. It only gets dropped when the identifier happens to start with the same prefix as internal system tags.

Activity logs marked as staff-visible are hidden from staff but shown to regular users
Activity entries configured with a staff-only visibility setting are appearing in the activity log for regular users instead of being restricted. The same entries are correctly hidden from staff members. The visibility filter that should allow staff to see these entries while hiding them from non-staff users is inverted.

Dashboard variable nullability lost after override
When I set a dashboard variable to null and then apply an override, the variable ends up with a value instead of remaining null. The same override works correctly through the model-based code path but silently drops the null flag in the dict-based path.

Overriding start date clears the end date
When I override just the start date on a dashboard tile, the end date becomes blank, ignoring the dashboard's original end date. I expected the dashboard's end date to still apply when only the start date is overridden.

Nested OR property groups lose their logic when combined with AND filters
When I apply dashboard filters that include an OR group nested inside an AND group, the OR relationship disappears and all conditions are treated as AND. For example, if I set up a filter to match users where email is X AND (country is US OR country is UK), the query only returns users matching both US and UK simultaneously, which is impossible. I expected the OR grouping to be preserved.

Feature flags product shows as activated before any audience targeting is set up
I created two feature flags for my team using only basic rollout percentages with no audience segments. Despite having zero audience-based targeting rules, the feature flags product still shows as activated in our dashboard. I expected activation to require at least some audience-based targeting to be configured on the flags.

Data warehouse activation incorrectly reported for my team
My organization never created any custom data visualizations, yet the system shows our product intent as activated for the data warehouse feature. The activation appears to be counting visualization nodes created by a different team in the same project rather than only our own team's activity.

Product analytics activation stuck despite creating insights and dashboards
A team has created five insights and two dashboards, all by logged-in users, but the product analytics intent never transitions to activated. The activation check appears to gate on whether the team has ingested events, and that flag may not be set even though event data is flowing into the system.

Slot assignment changes don't take effect immediately
After updating my column-to-property mappings in the dashboard, the old mapping persists for many minutes before the system reflects the change. I've refreshed the page multiple times and waited, but the previous assignment keeps showing up. I expected updates to appear within seconds like other settings do.

Slot assignment inserts may create duplicates
When the weekly backfill populates the slot assignments table, some teams occasionally see duplicate entries for the same slot index after a reload. This appears to happen when multiple hosts write concurrently and the auto-generated version timestamps end up identical, causing the merge engine to keep both rows instead of collapsing to the latest one.

Cohort membership shows duplicate or stale entries
After a cohort is recalculated, some users appear multiple times in the results, and others who should no longer qualify remain listed. The issue resolves after waiting for background merges to complete, but it causes incorrect cohort sizes to be reported in the meantime.

User-edited column descriptions get overwritten
I edited a column description manually through the UI, but then when my automation script tried to create the same annotation again, my custom description was replaced with the default one. The field says user-edited annotations are never overwritten, but they clearly can be when the create endpoint is called on an existing row.

Editing an annotation doesn't mark it as user-edited
When I edit an existing annotation's description, the new text saves correctly but the annotation still shows as AI-generated instead of user-edited. Automated processes can overwrite my edits because the user-edited flag was never set.

Column validation rejects valid columns from recently updated tables
I added a new column to a warehouse table and immediately tried to annotate it, but the API returned a 400 saying the column doesn't exist. The column is definitely there — I can see it in the warehouse UI — but the validation seems to be comparing against cached table metadata that hasn't been refreshed since the column was added.

Query parameter values containing curly braces break query preparation
When I run a batch export with an exclude events filter that contains curly brace characters (for example, a JSON-like event filter expression), the query preparation fails because the formatting step interprets those braces as format placeholders. The error occurs during the string substitution phase before the query ever reaches the database.

Streaming JSON query silently stops on first malformed line
When iterating over results from the streaming JSON query method, the iteration abruptly stops after encountering a single line with invalid JSON. All rows after that bad line are lost with no warning or error message explaining why the stream ended early.

I was processing a large result set in batches and expected to receive all matching records. Instead, the loop completed after only a fraction of the expected rows, with no exception raised—just a clean end to iteration.

List column values appear as curly-brace arrays in CSV exports
When exporting batch records to CSV format, any column containing list values is rendered using PostgreSQL array syntax with curly braces instead of proper CSV formatting. For example, a field that should contain multiple items appears as a single value wrapped in curly braces, making the exported files difficult to parse and import into spreadsheet tools.

MySQL tables disappear from the warehouse after syncing
In direct-query mode, I noticed that some of my synced tables get soft-deleted on every refresh even though they still exist in the source database and haven't been removed from discovery. The tables were working fine before but suddenly show as stale. I expected the sync to recognize them as already-matched and leave them alone.

Direct query table shows no columns after saving column picker
After selecting columns in the column picker and saving, the live query table displays zero columns and queries fail. This happens even though I've explicitly selected columns. A full re-sync fixes the issue, but I shouldn't have to do that just to update column selections.

Investigation agent ignores invalid final report and keeps running
When the investigation agent submits a final report that doesn't match the required format, the system logs the validation error but then continues executing other tool calls and gives the agent another turn instead of stopping or telling the agent what was wrong. The agent eventually exhausts its budget without producing a usable report, even though it already attempted to submit one. I expected the agent to either accept the corrected report on retry or return whatever partial report it had.

Investigation agent runs out of tool calls too quickly
The anomaly investigation agent stops gathering information after only a few successful queries, even though the tool call budget should allow for more. Some of the agent's tool calls fail due to query errors or invalid parameters, but those failures still count against the total budget, leaving the agent with no remaining calls to investigate further.

Investigation continues running tools after the report submission fails validation
When the agent submits an investigation report that doesn't pass validation, the system still executes all the other tool calls that were in the same batch before telling the agent to fix its report. This wastes context tokens and confuses the model — it sees a mix of tool results alongside a "report rejected" message. I expected the agent to immediately get feedback about the invalid report without the extra noise of unrelated tool outputs.

Upload completion returns 201 Created even when nothing was uploaded
When I re-run an upload against a directory that has already been fully processed, the endpoint returns HTTP 201 Created despite no new files being created. I expected a 200 OK response since the upload process completed without creating anything new.

Delete returns not found for other failures
When I try to delete a symbol set, I sometimes get a 'not found' error even though the item is there. The error doesn't tell me why the deletion failed—it just says the symbol set wasn't found.

Multipart flag ignored when set to false
When I set the multipart flag to false on the legacy upload endpoint, the server still expects a multipart file upload. The request fails because the client sends raw file data, but the server tries to read from the multipart form fields.

Cached query results show data from warehouse tables I don't have access to
When I run a dashboard that includes a saved view, I can see rows from a warehouse table that my role should be blocked from reading. Another user with broader warehouse access ran the same dashboard first, and their cached results are being served to me on subsequent runs. I expected the cache to be partitioned by warehouse table access so denied users never see allowed users' cached data.

Dashboard views sometimes return stale data after a colleague's query runs
When I open a dashboard that uses saved warehouse views, I occasionally see results from a colleague's run instead of mine. The problem started after we began referencing saved queries with the models. prefix. I expect my own query results, scoped to my warehouse access, but the cached output from another user leaks through.
When I restore a deleted item to a specific folder, the item comes back but appears in its original location instead of the destination folder I chose.

Undo message appears after deletion even though undo is unavailable
When I delete an item and the system reports the operation was not undoable, I still see a message telling me how to undo it. The undo button stays disabled, so the message is misleading. I expected no undo message when the action cannot be reversed.

Trash shows item but restore button is missing
I moved a resource to the trash and went back to restore it, but the restore option was gone. The item was still listed in the trash like it had been soft-deleted, so I expected to be able to bring it back.

Cancelled queries keep running
When I cancel a running query from the interface, the query continues executing until it times out. The cancellation confirmation appears to succeed, but the query never actually stops. I expected the query to halt immediately after I request cancellation.

Query returns error even though results are displayed
When I run a query with very specific filters that match zero rows, the response shows my empty results but also includes an error message saying "Unknown error". The data comes back fine — there just aren't any matching rows — but the error indicator makes it look like something went wrong. I expected the query to complete successfully with empty results and no error.

UNION query branches each capped at default row limit
When running a query combining multiple SELECT statements with UNION, each individual branch is independently capped at the default row limit instead of just the final combined result. A UNION of several queries that would each return dozens of rows only returns a small fraction of the expected total.

Logs query byte limit silently ignored
When I run a query against a logs table, the configured maximum bytes to read isn't applied. The query proceeds without hitting the expected byte ceiling, potentially scanning far more data than intended.

Product limits can be modified by any admin user
Any staff account with access to the admin panel can change product limits for any organization, even ones they shouldn't have access to. The action succeeds without verifying the user has billing-related permissions. Only users with explicit billing authorization should be able to trigger or remove quota limits.

Slack destination workspace ID silently disappears after saving
I configured a Slack alert destination with a valid workspace and channel, and the setup completed without any error. But when I went back to edit it, the workspace ID field was blank — as if the configuration had never been saved. Reloading the page didn't bring it back either. I expected the workspace ID to persist across saves and edits.

Property set once gets overwritten during reconciliation
When processing person properties in windowed mode, I've seen a property that should have been set once (like an email address) get its value overwritten by a later set operation. The set once value was applied first but then immediately replaced by the set value for the same key. This only happens when both a set and a set once operation target the same property key within the same reconciliation run, which seems to occur when events span multiple time windows.

I expected the set once semantics to be preserved — if a property was flagged as set once, it shouldn't be silently overwritten by a concurrent set operation for the same key.

Input dependency ordering is wrong
When I save a workflow with multiple inputs that reference each other, the saved input order doesn't respect the declared dependencies — inputs get executed before the values they need. I set up input A to depend on input B, but B appears after A in the saved order instead of before it.

Valid subtractions rejected as hyphenated identifiers
When saving a configuration that subtracts one numeric field from another, the system rejects it with a message saying hyphens aren't supported in identifiers and suggests using bracket notation. The expression doesn't contain any hyphenated names—it's just plain arithmetic. I expected the save to succeed.

Hog code compiler hides specific error messages
When my Hog code fails to compile, I only ever see the generic message 'Hog code has errors' regardless of what actually went wrong. Whether it's a syntax mistake, an unsupported function call, or a reference to an unavailable variable, the compiler swallows the real error and gives me the same unhelpful message every time. I can't tell what's wrong with my code or how to fix it.

Modifier setting disappears after saving
I set a modifier through the API and it saved successfully, but when I fetch the project settings again the modifier is gone. It only happens with one specific modifier key — all others persist normally. I expected my configuration to be stored as-is.

URL regex patterns for session recording triggers pass validation but fail at query time
When I configure trigger groups for session recording with URL-based conditions, some regex patterns are accepted during setup but then fail when queries run against ClickHouse. The API validates URL patterns using Python's standard regex engine while ClickHouse uses re2 — the two engines differ in supported syntax, so a pattern that passes the API's validation can be rejected by the database. I expected the API to reject incompatible patterns upfront.

Linked flag settings won't save for session recording
When I try to configure a linked flag to trigger session recordings, the API rejects my changes and won't accept any linked flag configuration, even when I provide the required id and key fields correctly. It seems like no linked flag setup is ever accepted.

Property labels mix lowercase and uppercase inconsistently
When browsing person properties, some labels have fully lowercase property names like latest browser while others keep the first word capitalized, producing latest UTM source. The mixed casing makes the property picker look unpolished.

Filter listing empties on second call
When I request the list of available filters for the AI assistant, the result appears correctly the first time but returns nothing on subsequent calls. I'm building a debug view that needs to display the same list twice, but it works the first time and comes back empty the next. I expected the listing to be repeatable.

API keys endpoint doesn't require proper authorization
I could pull up another team member's API key configuration without the standard read permission. All the other endpoints for viewing member info require the proper scope, but this one appears to skip that check.

Two-factor authentication status lags behind actual setup
After completing the two-factor authentication setup, members don't immediately appear as having it enabled on the team members page. The status only updates after the authenticator app entry is confirmed in the database, leaving a window where the member appears unprotected despite having gone through the full setup flow.

Organization member visibility restrictions don't always apply
When an org disables member visibility, non-admin users should only see their project's members. Instead, some users can browse the full member list. I expected the directory to only show people on my team.

AI training data not deleted for some people after bulk deletion
When I delete a batch of people, some of them still have their AI training data left behind. I noticed this because a few days later I saw replay events still being scanned for distinct IDs belonging to people I had already removed. It seems like only some of the people in the batch are affected — the ones that happen to come after a few others that failed.

I expected all deleted people's training data to be cleared, regardless of whether one or two in the batch had issues.

Training deletion queued before person is actually deleted
When I delete a person, the AI training system receives a deletion request even if the person deletion fails partway through. The person remains in the system but the training pipeline still tries to remove their data, causing errors and orphaned deletion jobs.

I expected the training deletion to be queued only after the person is successfully deleted, or not queued at all if the deletion fails.

End-of-day filter includes events past the boundary
When I set an end-of-day filter to 23:59:59, events occurring later that second with fractional seconds still appear in my results. I expected the filter to stop exactly at 23:59:59.

End-of-hour detection misses sub-second timestamps
When querying event data with timestamps that have fractional seconds at the end of an hour (like 14:59:59.5), the system does not recognize them as end-of-hour values. This causes queries that should include those events to exclude them, resulting in incomplete hourly breakdowns. Timestamps at the exact second boundary work fine, but anything with fractional seconds is missed.

Silently dropped writes to deprecated fields
When I assign a value to a deprecated field in my model instance, the assignment appears to succeed—no exception is raised—but the value is never persisted. Only a deprecation warning is emitted, which I missed. I expected either the write to work or an explicit error telling me the field is read-only.

Migration detection fails with pre-subcommand flags
Running a management command with options before the action, such as a configuration flag, causes the system to treat it as a normal run rather than a migration. Deprecated fields turn into placeholders during the migration instead of staying intact, which can break the migration process.

Deprecated field returns None breaking downstream code
After wrapping a field with the deprecation helper, code that reads the field started failing because it gets None instead of the expected value. The database still has the data, but any logic depending on reading the field now breaks.

Passkey session data not cleared when providing a password
If I previously started a passkey registration but then decided to sign up with a password instead, the signup fails with an email mismatch error. The passkey credential from my earlier attempt lingers in the session and forces email-matching validation even though I'm using password authentication.

Reasoning request silently drops evaluations
When I ask for reasoning across a list of evaluations, some disappear from the results with no explanation. The response contains fewer items than I requested, but there is no flag or message indicating which ones were skipped or why. I expected either all requested evaluations to be returned, or at least an explicit marker on missing ones so I can distinguish data gaps from actual results.

Backfill total record count shows null after completion
When a batch export backfill finishes, the total record count sometimes displays as null in the backfill details, even though the backfill was estimated to have thousands of records. This happens when all individual batch runs fail — the system tries to calculate actual totals from completed runs, finds none, and replaces the valid estimate with null instead of keeping it.

Backfill silently drops data at the end of the range
When the backfill period doesn't divide evenly by the batch interval, the final partial interval is skipped and its data is never exported. A three-hour backfill with one-hour batches only exports two hours.

Backfill exports data from before the requested start time
I requested a backfill starting at a specific date, but the exported data includes records from several days earlier. The system appears to adjust the backfill start based on when data first exists, but it can shift the start backward instead of forward, pulling in unintended historical data.
Expected: Backfill should only export data within the requested time range.

Conversion attribution records vanish after seven days
Conversion attribution data disappears automatically one week after it's created, even though the associated events are still active in the system. I expected the preaggregated attribution data to persist as long as the underlying conversion events exist, not on a fixed seven-day schedule.

Team-level conversion attribution queries are unexpectedly slow
Queries that aggregate conversion attribution data by team take much longer than expected, while point queries for individual people are fast. I expected team-level queries to perform similarly to other attribution tables in our setup.

Internal fields leak into wildcard queries
When I run a wildcard query on the events table, I get extra columns that aren't part of the documented schema. These internal fields clutter dashboards and break tools that expect a fixed set of columns.

Group subtable asterisk expansion exposes internal columns
When I expand all columns from a group subtable in my query, internal storage columns appear alongside the expected group fields. I expected the asterisk expansion to only return public group fields, not internal implementation details.

Person details on an event don't match the person's actual profile
When I open an event and look at the associated person's information, the person's email and name are different from what I see when I visit that person's profile page directly. The person ID is correct, but the properties displayed on the event page are stale or come from a different source.

Rollout percentage false not recognized as full rollout
When a feature flag has its rollout percentage set to false, the flag is not included in the persisted flags list. I expected false to be treated the same as null, meaning the flag should be fully rolled out and cached.

Share percentages blank when start date is hidden behind a filter
I scanned a dashboard insight that uses a date filter expression, and the range and project share percentages were both blank. Other queries without a hidden start date show normal percentages. I expected the shares to still show how much data was read relative to the project.

Event filter suggestion appears for small queries but not large ones
I ran a query that reads almost all my events and received no warning about the missing event filter. A different query that only touches a few events did trigger the suggestion. I expected the warning to fire for the large read where it would matter most.

Expensive persons join not flagged when table metadata is unavailable
When the background metadata query that reads system parts fails, the scan stops warning about costly persons joins entirely. The same query gets flagged correctly when metadata is available. I expected the scan to still catch expensive joins even without table statistics.

Auto-approve blocked at exactly the displayed limit
I submitted a data deletion request for 100,000 events and unchecked the manual-review checkbox since the UI says requests under 100,000 events get auto-approved. The request never got approved and stayed pending — when I checked the log it said "100,000 matching events is at or above the 100,000 limit". I expected a request with exactly 100,000 events to be within the auto-approve threshold.

Auto-approval sweep gets stuck on one request and blocks all others
I submitted several data deletion requests and they all sat in "pending" for hours, even though some should have been auto-approved. Eventually the small ones got through but only after the broken one was manually deleted from the queue. It looks like one failing request monopolized the approval job every 30 minutes.

Expected: requests that can't be evaluated should not block the rest of the queue from being processed.

Stats refresh fails after approving a request
After approving a data deletion request, clicking Refresh Stats shows an error that the request changed while stats were being computed. The approval action updates the record's timestamp, which trips the conflict guard even though nothing else was edited. The freshly computed stats are discarded and I have to retry.

Delivery status check ignores the alert and team identifiers
I call the delivery status function with a specific team and alert identifier, and it always returns success as long as the message queue accepted the event. The team and alert parameters are passed in but never actually checked — even if I query for a completely different alert, the result is the same. I expected the function to confirm whether that particular alert's notification reached its destinations, not just whether the broker accepted the message.

API keys still visible in saved destination details
When I open a destination I already saved, my Slack token or webhook secret shows up in plain text instead of being masked. I expected the system to hide all credentials when displaying stored destinations.

Alert check results fail to store with encoding error
Saving alert check results sometimes crashes with a JSON encoding error. Delivery receipts carry timestamp objects that aren't converted to strings, so the serializer rejects them.

Date argument interpreted incorrectly
When I pass a date in a non-standard format to the command, the reports are generated for the wrong day. The help text says to use YYYY-MM-DD format, but the command silently accepts other formats and parses them ambiguously.

Async runs lock out future dispatches even when the background task fails
I ran the command with --async and saw "Queued!", but when I tried to rerun it later for the same date I got an error saying the date was already dispatched. The background task had actually failed silently, so the lock was held forever and no new runs could proceed for that day.

Scan results vanish intermittently after appearing
I trigger a scan for a slow query and the analysis shows up on the dashboard, but on the next request the results vanish until I reload the page. It comes back on subsequent loads. This makes the performance insights unreliable.

Scan jobs stop being enqueued after a Redis hiccup
After a brief Redis connection issue, no new scan jobs were enqueued for our project even though queries were running slowly. Other projects' scans continued normally. We had to wait over a minute before scans resumed.

Stale scan blocks new analysis
When a query scan hangs or crashes while pending, subsequent requests for the same query never trigger a new scan. The query stays showing "scanning..." until the old pending entry expires, forcing users to wait unnecessarily.

Background jobs rejected immediately when concurrency limit is reached
When running background jobs, I noticed that tasks are being rejected as soon as the concurrency limit is hit, with no attempt to wait for a slot to become available. Other parts of the system will retry and wait, so I expected the same behavior here. This causes more task failures during peak load than necessary.

Organization concurrency limit doesn't update after plan change
After upgrading our plan to increase the concurrent query limit, queries were still being blocked by the old limit. I had to wait a long time before the new limit started applying. I expected the updated limit to take effect immediately after the plan change.

App-level concurrency limit has no retry mechanism
When concurrent queries from the same organization exceed the concurrency limit, they fail immediately rather than waiting for a slot to open up. This leads to intermittent query failures during peak usage, even though other throttling mechanisms in the system gracefully retry before failing.

Absolute threshold alerts run slower than expected
Even when I set up a simple check against a fixed value, the system fetches data from both the current and previous time periods. Only the current period is needed to compare against the threshold, so this adds unnecessary latency to every evaluation.

Alert notifications show "empty result" as the metric name
When my alert triggers on an insight that returned no data for the interval, the breach message refers to the metric as "empty result" instead of the actual insight or series name. It's confusing because the notification looks like it's describing something that doesn't exist rather than the real metric I set up.

Alerts recalculate every time instead of using cached results
My daily insight alerts run full calculations on every check even though the underlying data hasn't changed. I expected the system to skip re-computation when the cache is still fresh.

Unique event counts are zero during session data backfill
