Field cannot be updated by alias
When I try to update a field using its alias as the key, I get an error saying the field name doesn't match, even though the field exists and I can retrieve it using the same alias. I expected to be able to update fields by their name or alias, consistent with how I can read them.

Shutdown callback silently skipped in synchronous mode
I registered a cleanup callback with the shutdown monitor, expecting it to execute when the worker begins shutting down. But when using the synchronous context manager, the callback is silently skipped and never runs. I expected the callback to fire regardless of whether I use the async or sync version of the context manager.

Retryable shutdown error becomes a runtime error
During graceful worker shutdown, activities fail with a generic runtime error instead of the expected retryable shutdown error. This happens when the shutdown notification is raised but the activity context is no longer available, preventing proper retries.

Shutdown signal takes a full second to register
When the orchestrator sends a termination signal, the worker doesn't start cleaning up until about a second later. I was scaling down a pod and noticed the shutdown wasn't immediate even though the signal was received. I expected the worker to begin its graceful shutdown almost right away.

Query row limit silently capped during execution
When I set a high row limit on my query, the system silently reduces it without any warning. My results contain fewer rows than I asked for, and there's no indication that the limit was changed. Lower limits work as expected, but once I go above a certain threshold, my query is silently truncated.

Metrics server stays alive after worker crashes
When a worker task fails and the process exits, the metrics HTTP server that was started alongside it keeps running in the background, holding onto its port and consuming memory. I expected the metrics endpoint to shut down together with the worker so resources are fully reclaimed.

Histogram bucket overrides silently dropped for certain task queues
We deployed a worker for a new task queue type and noticed the latency histograms use default bucket ranges instead of the custom ones we configured. Other task queues show the expected buckets, but this one falls back to the defaults. We expected the worker setup to apply the appropriate histogram bucket overrides for all recognized task queues.

JSON length returns null for object values
Measuring the length of a JSON field returns null whenever the value is an object, though arrays work fine and return the correct count. I expected the same behavior for both types.

Random function ignores seed argument
When I pass a seed value to the random number function to get reproducible results, the seed is silently ignored and each query returns different random values. I expected the function to respect the seed for consistent results across runs.

Raw JSON extraction returns variant type instead of text
When extracting raw JSON content from a field, the result comes back as a structured variant instead of plain text. This causes type errors when the extracted value is used in string operations like concatenation or comparison. Other JSON extraction functions correctly return strings, making this behavior inconsistent and unexpected.

Drain stops for a sweep and never resumes
After the cleanup job pauses because a ClickHouse sweep starts, it stays stopped forever even though the sweep finishes within minutes. Queue rows pile up and are never deleted until someone manually restarts the job. I expected the drain to resume once the sweep was done.

Last-success timestamp refreshed on timed-out runs
I set up alerting on the last-success metric and it never fires, but the drain has been falling behind for days. The timestamp keeps updating whenever the drain hits its time limit and exits, so the alert thinks it is healthy while the queue grows.

Local S3 queries for web analytics always hit the wrong bucket
When I run locally, queries for web analytics data always target a hardcoded bucket name rather than using the same bucket configured for production. If I change the production bucket, my local environment keeps pointing at the old one and fails. The local URL construction should respect the production bucket setting.

S3 web stats export missing dimension columns
When I query the daily web analytics S3 export table, I only get period bucket, team ID, and raw aggregate counts — no hostname, device type, page path, or geographic data. The regular in-app web analytics table shows all those dimensions, so I expected the S3 export to include them too. Without them I can't break down traffic by browser, country, or referring source.

Web bounces table returns no data
When I query the web bounces analytics table built from S3, it returns zero rows even though I can see pageviews in the regular stats table. The bounces and session duration columns are missing from the results entirely. I expected the bounces table to show bounce counts and session durations alongside the standard metrics.

Bulk embedding insert crashes on empty input
Calling the bulk embedding creation function with an empty list still attempts to run an INSERT statement with no values, which causes a database syntax error. I expected the function to handle empty input gracefully and simply do nothing.

Removal count inflated in activity log
Moving an insight between dashboards sometimes logs more removals than I made. If an insight was previously removed from a dashboard and later re-added, removing it again records an extra removal for the old dashboard alongside the actual one.

Restored insight reappears on dashboards it was removed from
When I restore a deleted insight, it shows up again on dashboards I had previously removed it from. I expected restoring an insight to only bring back its original placement, not resurrect tiles I'd intentionally taken off dashboards.

Tiles created on unexpected dashboards
When placing an insight on multiple dashboards at once, the tiles sometimes end up on dashboards that weren't in the original request. I pass a list of dashboard IDs, get back a placement plan, and then apply it — but the resulting tiles include dashboards I never asked for. I expected the placement to only touch the dashboards I specified.

title: Tiles created on unexpected dashboards
body: When placing an insight on multiple dashboards at once, the tiles sometimes end up on dashboards that weren't in the original request. I pass a list of dashboard IDs, get back a placement plan, and then apply it — but the resulting tiles include dashboards I never asked for. I expected the placement to only touch the dashboards I specified.

Async views losing session data
I have an async view that modifies session data, but the changes don't stick. After the request completes, the session data is back to its original state. Regular sync views work fine.

Newly created sessions missing activity timestamp
Sessions created through the async path don't have a last activity timestamp set, showing as blank in the admin panel. Sessions created through the synchronous path work fine. I expected all newly created sessions to have an activity timestamp recorded.

Logged-in user's session loses its user ID
After logging in, subsequent requests treat the session as anonymous. Page views and events stop being attributed to my account and show up under 'Anonymous' instead. Relogging fixes it temporarily, but the problem returns on the next session. The session data still contains my authentication credentials.

Custom integrations disappear after running the template sync command
After running the template synchronization command, several of my custom integrations vanished from the interface. They had been working properly before, but the sync process removed them even though they should still be active. I expected the command to update existing templates without deleting any that are still in use.

Logs queries ignore property groups setting
When running a logs query with property groups explicitly disabled, the query still uses optimized property groups anyway. The configuration I set has no effect for logs workloads — it gets silently overridden. I expected my explicit setting to be respected like it is for other query types.

Password rejected after being entered exactly as provided
I received a newly generated password from my colleague to access a shared dashboard. I copied the password character for character into the prompt, but every attempt was denied. Refreshing the page and trying again produced the same result. Other passwords for different shared resources work without issue.

Password update doesn't persist after changing it
When I update the password for a shared dashboard, the change appears to go through, but after refreshing the page the old password still works. I have to create an entirely new password entry instead of being able to modify the existing one.

Digest remains enabled for other organizations
I disabled the error tracking digest for a user by providing their email along with an organization ID. The user stopped receiving digests for that organization's projects, but they still receive digests for projects in other organizations they belong to. I expected the digest to be fully disabled for the user.

Digest disable preview shows inflated project count
When previewing changes before applying the bulk digest disable for an organization, the tool says it will disable the digest for every project in the org. But some users already have it turned off for certain projects, so fewer changes will actually be made. The preview count is higher than reality.

Overlapping regex filters produce empty results
When I add a regex filter and a not-regex filter on the same property, the system only flags them as conflicting if the two patterns are character-for-character identical. If the excluded pattern covers everything the first filter would match, the filters are treated as compatible and the query returns no results.

Null entries in value arrays become the literal text "None"
When a property filter includes null inside its value array, it gets turned into the string "None" instead of being skipped. This makes the filter match against the literal word None and can cause false conflicts with other filters on the same property.

LLM signal exceeds token limit
I noticed that some error tracking signals sent to the LLM are being rejected due to exceeding the maximum token length. The signal should be trimmed before sending, but it appears the token counting and the trimming use different encodings, so the final trimmed message can still go over the limit.

I was looking at error reports where the signal was delivered but the LLM returned an error about input length. I expected all signals to stay within the configured token budget.

Copying a resource produces '(Copy 2)' even when '(Copy 1)' is available
When I duplicate a resource whose name already exists in the destination team, the system sometimes skips '(Copy 1)' and assigns '(Copy 2)' instead. This happens whenever a bare '(Copy)' suffix is already taken — the deduplication logic then starts checking numbered copies from two and never considers one.

Folded record count exceeds unique memberships in output state
After running a reconciliation fold, the number of folded records is higher than the total unique person-cohort pairs in the resulting state. Replayed messages with older timestamps pass validation and are counted as folded even though they're silently ignored because a newer record is already present. I expected the folded count to match the actual number of records in the output.

Timestamp parsing rejects valid values with trailing whitespace
Valid records are being silently dropped during the fold because their timestamps include trailing whitespace that prevents the parsing step from recognizing them. The timestamps are otherwise correct, but the parsing doesn't trim the whitespace before matching. The drop count for unrecognized records is higher than expected, and the issue affects a consistent subset of records.

Completeness flag never reports true
Even after all partitions have been recorded for a reconcile run, the completeness check still returns false. I expected it to confirm completion once every partition has been seen.

Conditional lazy field access breaks when field is in the else branch
I'm querying with an if expression that conditionally accesses a field from a related table — something like checking a status and returning a field from the joined table in both branches. When the lazy-joined field appears in the else branch of the if, the query fails as if that table was never joined. It works fine when the field is only in the true/then branch. I expected both branches to resolve correctly since the join should be added regardless of which branch uses the field.

Wrapped lazy table subquery fails with unknown column error
When a lazy table gets wrapped in a subquery due to circular dependencies, the subquery tries to select internal tracking identifiers as column names instead of actual field names. Queries fail with an unknown column error when accessing properties on these lazy tables.

Properties on lazy tables silently dropped in non-standard query flows
When accessing properties on lazy tables from non-standard query entry points, the properties are silently skipped during resolution. Regular field accesses on the same lazy tables work fine, but property-based access fails. This prevents building reports and dashboards that rely on lazy table properties through alternative query paths.

Deprecation warning not shown for feature flag events in subqueries
My query compared the event column to the feature flag called event inside a subquery, but I never received the deprecation warning about migrating to the flag evaluations table. The query ran without any warnings and only after reading documentation did I learn the pattern would stop working.

Migration warning missing for exclusion queries
When I exclude the feature flag called event from my results using a NOT IN clause, I don't see the migration warning. But when I include it with IN, the warning appears. I expected to see the warning regardless of whether I'm including or excluding the event.

Deprecation warning missing when query uses a saved view
My query references a saved view that filters on feature flag events, but I never see the deprecation warning telling me to migrate. The warning does show up on similar queries that don't use a saved view. I expected to be warned either way so I could update my queries before the old table is removed.

Newly created web experiments don't appear in my web experiments list
When I create a new experiment from the web experiments interface, it saves successfully but then never shows up in the list of web experiments. I have to go into the experiment settings and manually change its type to web before it appears. I expected creating an experiment through the web experiments path to automatically mark it as a web-type experiment so it shows up right away.

Invalid field values pass validation
The funnel validator accepts invalid field values. I can enter a table name with special characters or a timestamp field that doesn't exist. Queries fail later with unclear errors.

Only one complexity limit error shown when both are exceeded
When I configure a data warehouse funnel with too many steps AND too many distinct tables, only the step count error is displayed. The distinct table limit check is never reached because the function returns early after detecting too many steps. I expected both issues to be reported together so I could fix all problems at once.

Site app defaults don't apply when config is empty
When I save a site app configuration without setting any optional fields, all settings show as blank on the next page load instead of using the predefined defaults. I expect the schema defaults to populate automatically.

Site app URLs don't change after republishing
After updating and republishing my site app, the decide endpoint returns the exact same URL as before. Because the URL hasn't changed, my browser loads the cached old version instead of the new code. I expected a new URL each time I republished so that browsers would fetch the latest version.

Site app fails to load after deployment
After deploying a new version of my site app, the app doesn't appear in the browser for several seconds. The plugin config shows as enabled and the deployment appears successful, but the app is completely invisible to visitors until the build step finishes.

Cached data persists after copying an insight tile to another dashboard
When I copy an insight tile to a different dashboard, the new dashboard shows stale cached results instead of freshly computed data. The cache was already populated on the original dashboard, and after copying the tile the old cached values are still displayed.

Tiles appear in unexpected order on dashboard
After rearranging tiles on a dashboard and saving, reloading the page shows them in a different order than I arranged. I expected them to stay in the positions I set, with tiles ordered by their layout coordinates.

Tile vanishes when moving between dashboards
I moved a chart tile from one dashboard to another using the move action, but after the operation completed the tile was gone from both dashboards. The move appeared to succeed with no error, yet the tile simply disappeared instead of showing up on the destination dashboard.

Expected the tile to appear on the target dashboard after the move completes.

HTML report omits py-spy profiling data
When I generate both a markdown and HTML migration profile report and include py-spy raw sampling files, the HTML report is missing the Python hot functions section that appears in the markdown version. The markdown report shows the sampled call stacks and flame graph links, but the HTML version skips this entirely.

Hog function call count is wrong for teams with both succeeded and failed calls
When a team has both successful and failed hog function invocations in a billing period, the reported total is incorrect — it only shows the count for one of the two metric types instead of the combined total. I expected the usage report to sum succeeded and failed calls together, as the query filters on both metric types with an IN clause.

Feature flag request counts show zero after adding a new cloud region
After deploying to a new cloud region, the usage reports started showing zero feature flag requests even though we're actively using them. The billing dashboard for this metric stays blank while other metrics populate normally.

Scheduled data pipelines keep running after team is deleted
After deleting a team, its automated data modeling workflows still trigger in the background. The team's data is gone but the scheduled tasks continue to run and fail against missing resources.

Loop schedules keep firing after team deletion
I deleted a team but its scheduled loops continued running, throwing errors because the underlying data no longer existed. I expected all schedules tied to that team to stop immediately.

Team deletion fails with unhelpful recursion error
When deleting a team, the operation fails with an error about a recursion limit being exceeded. The message says to repair the problematic row, but it doesn't identify which row or which model is causing the issue. There's no way to determine what needs fixing without manually inspecting the database.

OAuth token revoked without notification email
After my OAuth application token was exposed publicly, it stopped working but I never received the security alert email about the revocation. I only discovered the problem when one of my integrations suddenly failed to authenticate. I expected to be notified as soon as the token was revoked so I could generate a replacement.

Leaked team token goes unrevoked when reported via API
When I report a leaked team secret token through the API, the system identifies it as a project secret API key because they share the same prefix. The subsequent lookup fails silently because team tokens aren't stored as project secret API keys. The token remains active despite my report, leaving my account vulnerable. I expected the token to be revoked or at least receive a message explaining why it couldn't be.

Key not actually revoked despite success message
After reporting my personal API key as leaked, the system confirmed the key was revoked and sent me a replacement. But the old key continued to work for authentication. I repeated the process and got the same result each time.

Retry delay exceeds configured maximum
Even though I set a cap on the retry delay, the actual wait time between attempts sometimes goes over that limit. I expected the delay to never exceed the maximum value I specified.

Batch export retries forever on subclassed error types
When a batch export fails with an error that inherits from a configured non-retryable error type, the export keeps retrying instead of failing immediately. The system only checks for exact error type matches, so subclasses are treated as retryable even when their parent class is listed as non-retryable. I expected errors matching the parent class to also be treated as non-retryable and stop the export.

Batch export crashes on certain field types
Running a batch export sometimes fails with a column count mismatch error when the data contains fields matching the JSON column names but stored as non-standard Arrow types rather than regular strings. The export works for standard fields but crashes on these edge cases. I expected the export to handle all field types gracefully without crashing.

Intermittent timeout detection failure
When a database query exceeds the allowed time, the system sometimes fails to recognize the timeout and lets the raw database error bubble up to the user. This happens inconsistently - sometimes the timeout is caught and handled gracefully, and sometimes it isn't. I expected all timeout errors to be handled the same way.

Nested property access produces invalid output
When I access a property on a complex expression, the generated HogQL is invalid. I expected the property chain to be constructed correctly.

Unclear error when a lazy join resolver is missing
When running a HogQL query that involves a table join, I get a confusing error about an unknown lazy join resolver. The error message tells me to add the resolver to a registry, but doesn't tell me which resolver tag is actually missing or what valid tags exist. I expected a clearer message that lists the known resolver tags so I could identify the mismatch.

Path gets corrupted when renaming a file with special characters
When I rename a file whose name contains a forward slash or backslash, the resulting path shows extra escape characters. The file appears with a mangled path in the directory listing, making it look like a completely different file from the original.

Path gets mangled after renaming a file or folder
When I rename a file or folder, the resulting path ends up with extra backslashes scattered through the name. Renaming other items in the same location works fine. I expected the name to update cleanly.

Outbound requests burst when Redis is down
When Redis becomes unavailable, my outbound webhook deliveries are no longer paced and are sent as fast as possible. I expected the rate limiter to continue applying at least basic pacing even during Redis outages to avoid overwhelming downstream services.

Rate limit budget consumed even when requests are denied
The outbound rate limiter seems to use up quota for calls that are ultimately rejected. After a burst of denials, the allowed send rate drops much faster than it should, as though the rejected requests also consumed tokens. Only accepted calls should reduce the available budget.

Pacing advice suggests waiting far too long between outbound calls
I'm sending requests at a steady rate well within my configured limit, but the system keeps telling me to wait much longer than necessary before making the next call. This creates unnecessary latency even though I haven't come close to hitting my rate limit. I expected the pacing advice to only recommend delays when I'm actually approaching the budget cap.

Backup job hangs indefinitely with no timeout
I scheduled an incremental backup and it has been running for over 14 hours with no progress update. The job never fails or reports an error — it just sits there forever. Other backups complete normally within a few hours. I expected the job to either finish or fail after a reasonable maximum duration, but it appears to have no upper bound on how long it will wait.

Full database backup job fails immediately saying a backup is already in progress
When I trigger a full database backup (without specifying a particular table), the job fails right away with an error claiming another backup for the same table is still running, even though no backup is actually in progress. Incremental backups for individual tables work fine. Full database backups have been completely broken since the concurrency check was added.

Evaluation report attempt count never increments after generation
After an evaluation report is generated and delivered, the system fails to record that an attempt was made. The attempt counter stays at its previous value instead of being incremented, making it impossible to track how many reports have been processed.

Per-report evaluation workflow crashes when started without parameters
When I trigger the per-report evaluation workflow without providing input parameters, it fails immediately before doing any work. Other workflows in the same scheduling system handle missing inputs gracefully by falling back to defaults. I expected this workflow to start normally with built-in defaults.

Fan-out failure log hides which reports actually failed
When a batch of evaluation reports fails during fan-out, the warning message is just a generic classification string. The report identifiers and error details are buried in the structured log extras field, making it difficult to quickly scan logs and identify which specific reports need attention.

Read-only validation rejects queries that only read data
I submitted a raw SQL query that begins with SELECT and only reads data, but it was rejected with an error claiming the statement isn't read-only. The query contains no INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE keywords, no external data access functions, and no query-level settings overrides. I expected it to execute normally since it's a straightforward read operation.

Direct query fails for non-cloud ClickHouse connections
When I try to use direct query with a regular ClickHouse source (not ClickHouse Cloud), the system rejects it with an invalid connection error even though the SSH tunnel and host are valid. The same setup works fine when the source is marked as ClickHouse Cloud.

I expected both ClickHouse Cloud and standard ClickHouse sources to be accepted, as long as they pass the capability and engine checks.

ClickHouse error messages are truncated to the first line
When a direct query fails, the error message shown contains only the first line of the original ClickHouse error. Detailed diagnostic information on subsequent lines is lost, making it hard to diagnose the underlying problem.

Comma-separated values not split when combined with repeated parameters
When I include both comma-separated IDs and repeated query parameters in the same request, the comma-separated portion isn't treated as multiple values and causes a validation error. I expected all IDs to be recognized regardless of how I formatted them.

Query parameters wrapped in square brackets are silently parsed as JSON arrays
When I pass a filter value that happens to be surrounded by square brackets — for example, a tag named [custom] — the API silently converts it into a two-element list instead of treating it as a literal string. I expected the brackets to be preserved as part of the value since I'm sending a single query parameter, not a JSON-encoded array.

Optional boolean filters default to false when omitted
When I leave an optional boolean filter parameter out of my request, the endpoint treats it as false rather than ignoring it. For example, omitting the impersonation filter returns only records where the actor was NOT impersonating, as if I had explicitly selected No instead of All. I expected that not providing the parameter would leave it unset and return all records.

Generated experiment data disappears from analytics dashboard
I ran the experiment data generation command for 2000 users and it reported success, but only a fraction of the events appear in the analytics dashboard. Some users' exposure events and action events are completely missing. I expected all generated events to show up since the command completes without errors.

Test data sent to wrong team when no team ID specified
When I run the experiment data generation command without providing a team ID, the tool sometimes sends events to an unexpected team. I expected it to either use my current team or fail gracefully, but instead it appears to grab the first available team in the database.

Funnel experiment step timing differs between variants
When I generate test data for a funnel experiment, the test group has a longer delay between signup started and signup completed than the control group. I expected the step timing to be identical across variants so that only the conversion rate differs. This makes it impossible to isolate the effect of the conversion rate improvement from the effect of the longer delay.

Session property value suggestions missing for hostname fields
When I try to filter sessions by the entry or exit hostname fields, the dropdown shows no available values to select from. Other URL-related properties like entry path or referring domain show a populated list, but the hostname fields come back empty. I expected all URL properties to show value suggestions the same way.

Bounce rate ignores sessions with autocapture events but no page views
When I check my bounce rate, sessions where users interacted with the page (clicked elements, scrolled) are excluded entirely if they didn't trigger a page view event. The bounce rate looks artificially high because these partially-engaged sessions don't count toward either bounces or non-bounces. I expected any session with user interaction to be classified as not-a-bounce rather than silently dropped from the calculation.

Session data missing when joining events to sessions
When I join the events table to the sessions table, many events show null for session fields like entry URL and channel type, even though those events clearly belong to active sessions. The issue only appears in the default query mode — when I switch to UUID join mode the same query returns correct session data for all events.

Issue status changes don't show up immediately after bulk updates
I changed the status of several issues in quick succession and my dashboard still showed the old statuses right away. The changes only appeared after waiting about a minute. I expected my most recent changes to be reflected immediately.

Expected instead: Recent status changes should appear right away without waiting for the background sync cycle.

Status updates don't show up consistently
After changing an issue's status, the new status sometimes appears in my results and sometimes doesn't, even though I waited the same amount of time. I expected the interface to always reflect my latest changes.

Person lookup by distinct IDs silently drops extra matches
When I look up a person using multiple distinct IDs (for example, an anonymous session ID and a logged-in email), only the first matched distinct ID is returned. The other distinct IDs that belong to the same person appear as if they have no matching person at all. I expected every distinct ID I sent to show up as matched on the correct person row.

Returns fewer results than distinct IDs queried
When I pass multiple distinct IDs that belong to the same person, the function returns only one person instead of one result per distinct ID. I expected to get back a result for each distinct ID I queried, even if some of them resolve to the same person.

Distinct IDs list cuts off for heavily merged accounts
When I look up a person who has been merged many times, their distinct IDs list stops after the first batch. I expected all their distinct IDs to be returned.

Issue creation fails with a misleading error when timestamps can't be parsed
When I try to create an issue from an event, the system sometimes errors out saying the exception timestamp is invalid, even though the event clearly exists. The error message doesn't indicate that a fallback timestamp was also tried and failed, so it's impossible to tell whether the problem is with the event data itself or the issue metadata. I expected a clearer message explaining that all available timestamps were unparseable.

Event properties not loading right after issue creation
When I create a new issue and immediately open its details, the event properties section shows nothing. The issue clearly exists and the underlying event is there — if I wait a moment and reload the page, the properties appear correctly. I expected them to be available as soon as the issue is created.

Event properties take much longer to load after data format change
After a recent change to how event data is stored, loading properties for older issues became noticeably slower. The system appears to hit the cache but can't use the data, then falls back to a slower source every time. Only after clearing the cache did things return to normal speed.

Stale properties returned when querying groups with a limit
When I query the groups table with a limit, I sometimes get outdated property values instead of the latest ones. After updating a company's name or industry, a limited query still shows the old values while an unlimited query returns the correct data. The deduplication logic that picks the most recent version of each group appears to exclude newer entries when the result set is capped.

Group properties vanish when query has a row limit
When I run a query with a row limit that accesses group properties, some events return blank group data while others display correctly. Running the same query without a row limit shows all group data. I expected the row limit to only control how many results are returned, not which group information is populated.

Group property joins take minutes even with tight date filters
When I join events with group properties like organization name, the query takes several minutes to complete even though I've filtered to a narrow date range with only a few matching events. The result set is tiny but the query seems to process every group record in the project. I expected the date filter to make this fast.

Custom rate limit override silently ignored
I set a custom hourly rate limit for a partner endpoint in the admin settings, but requests are still being throttled according to the default tier budget instead. The value appears to be saved, yet it has no effect on request handling.

Min and max aggregations fail on text properties
When I use min or max on a text property in an experiment, the query fails or returns incorrect results. Min and max should work directly on text values without requiring numeric conversion.

Scalar hash functions incorrectly classified as aggregations
When checking whether a function is an aggregation, scalar hash functions are incorrectly returned as aggregations. This causes downstream logic to treat them as aggregate operations when they should be scalar. I expected hash functions to be recognized as non-aggregations.

Traffic type shows bot for regular browsers on cloud IPs
When I look at my traffic type breakdown, requests from a standard browser user agent hosted on a cloud provider IP are showing up as bot instead of regular. I expected the classification to rely primarily on the user agent string, falling back to IP only when the user agent is ambiguous or missing.

Bot name lookup can't distinguish missing user agents from regular traffic
When I query for bot names in my HogQL queries, requests with no user agent return blank just like regular traffic. I can't filter out or identify which rows have a missing user agent versus those that are simply not bots. The function that returns traffic categories already distinguishes these cases, so I expected the same behavior here.

Non-browser requests show up as bots
When I filter my dashboard to exclude bot traffic, requests from our monitoring tools and API clients still appear in the bot category. These requests don't have a user agent header, but I expected them to be treated as regular traffic rather than flagged as bots.

Unexpected extra column in person distinct ID override queries
When querying the person distinct ID overrides table and requesting only specific columns, an additional identifier column appears in the results that was never asked for. This happens whether or not I'm joining to other tables. The query should return only the fields I explicitly requested.

Flag evaluations table missing from editor
The flag evaluations table doesn't appear in the HogQL editor even though I enabled the feature flag for my organization. My settings show the correct mode, but the table is still absent from autocomplete.

Salesforce enrichment can run twice at once
When the enrichment workflow takes longer than expected, a new run starts before the previous one finishes on Sunday. This leads to duplicate records being sent to Salesforce. Other Salesforce enrichment schedules prevent this by skipping overlapping runs.

One missing scheduled workflow blocks all others from registering
When I restart the server after deploying a new version, only some of the scheduled background jobs appear in the Temporal UI. It turns out that if any single schedule fails during startup, the rest are never registered at all. I expected every schedule to attempt registration independently, so that one failing job doesn't silently prevent dozens of others from running.

Weekly digest notification schedule runs on the wrong day and time
The weekly digest notification is supposed to fire on Monday mornings, but it actually runs on Thursday at 5 PM. I checked the schedule settings and saw it was configured for a completely different time than what was promised, causing notifications to arrive days late and at an inconvenient hour.

Survey cohort references left pointing to old organization after transfer
When I duplicate a survey into another workspace, some of its targeting cohorts remain linked to the original workspace's cohorts. The survey appears to transfer without error, but when I open it I see broken cohort references and can't edit the filters. Only the cohorts listed under the standard properties section get updated; any targeting criteria stored in other parts of the survey's conditions are skipped.

Cohort references in survey targeting not updated after transfer
When I transfer a survey to another organization, the cohort IDs embedded in the targeting conditions stay pointing to the original org's cohorts. The survey appears in the destination but its targeting silently stops working because those cohorts don't exist there.

I expected all cohort references inside the survey's conditions to be remapped to the newly duplicated cohorts in the destination organization.

Turning off recurrence leaves the repeat frequency set
When I update a recurring schedule to run only once, the repeat frequency keeps its old value. I expected clearing the recurrence setting to also remove the frequency so the change fires a single time.

Scheduled change rejected for valid flag
Attempting to schedule a change to modify a feature flag's configuration fails with an unsupported format error, even though the flag should be compatible.

Scheduled change bypasses approval requirement
When I create a scheduled change for a feature flag that normally triggers an approval request, no approval request appears and the schedule shows as ready to apply without waiting for anyone to approve it. I was scheduling a flag status change on a project with strict change controls, and I expected to see a pending approval request before the change could take effect.

Users without distinct IDs show up as "None" in analytics
When sending transactional emails to users who don't have a distinct ID configured, their activity shows up in analytics with the literal string "None" as their distinct ID instead of being omitted. I expected the system to skip the distinct ID entirely for such users.

Organization names with URL-like text become clickable links in email body
When my organization name contains something that looks like a web address, mail clients automatically underline and hyperlink it in the email body. Other parts of the system strip out those URL patterns to prevent auto-linking, but the rendered email still shows the raw text that clients treat as links.

Email failure count stuck at 1 for batch sends
When sending notification emails to multiple recipients at once, the Prometheus failure counter always increments by exactly one even if the entire batch fails. The monitoring dashboard shows only a single failure instead of the actual number of recipients that didn't receive their email.

I was doing a routine check of our alerting metrics and noticed the email failure time series never goes above 1 per event, even during incidents where dozens of emails bounced or timed out.

String array columns return empty string as default
When a string array column has no value, the system returns an empty string instead of an empty array. This causes type mismatches downstream since string operations are applied where array operations were expected.

Integer array fields return an empty string as default instead of an empty list
When querying an integer array column that has no value set, the default returned is an empty string rather than an empty array. This causes downstream expressions that expect an array to fail or behave unexpectedly.

Evaluation completes before the trace has finished arriving
I set my trace-target evaluation window to three hours, expecting the system to wait the full duration after the first generation before evaluating. Instead, the evaluation ran after only two hours and graded an incomplete trace. Longer window settings I configure appear to be silently capped at two hours.

Trace evaluation crashes on large traces
Evaluating a trace with many generations sometimes fails with an unhandled error instead of returning a verdict. The step that formats the trace for the automated reviewer crashes when the trace exceeds certain limits, preventing the entire evaluation from completing even though a degraded verdict would be preferable.

Rate limit change not taking effect
I changed the rate limit for a team in the settings, but queries from that team were still being allowed up to the old limit. I expected the new limit to apply immediately.

Series labels are indistinguishable when a formula combines multiple series
When an insight uses formulas to combine series, the metric description lists every series with the same "Input series" label. There is no way to tell which series are actually used as inputs in the formula versus other series that happen to be in the insight, so I cannot figure out what the formula is combining.

Hidden filter count doesn't add up
The 'X more filters not shown' message is often wrong. Some filters are silently dropped because they have no key set, but those don't get counted in the 'more' number, so visible filters plus the stated extra count falls short of the actual total.

Default data report shows created items that were only updated
When running the database setup command, the output lists the growth enrichment prompt config under 'Created defaults', but the record already existed in the database - it just hadn't been activated yet. The command only flipped its active status, so the 'Created' label is wrong and confusing.

Clipping warning appears for partitions that never had messages in the query window
When running the cohort parity check with a recent time threshold, some partitions show up in the potentially clipped warning even though they genuinely never produced any messages in the queried window. The tool flags these as potentially clipped by retention, but they simply had no data before the query start time. I expected the warning only for partitions where retention actually removed earlier messages.

After running a cohort membership parity check, the date reported for the oldest retained message is often weeks earlier than when messages actually appeared in the topic. I've seen it claim messages from months ago on topics that were only recently populated. I expected it to reflect when messages were actually ingested, not when they were originally authored.

Log query byte limit stuck at free tier for paid accounts
When running complex log queries, my account gets blocked with a max bytes exceeded error at the 50 GB threshold, even though we're on a paid plan. The query works fine when I simplify it to stay under 50 GB, but anything above that fails immediately instead of allowing up to 150 GB like our plan should support.

Kafka lag monitoring shows only the latest consumed timestamp per partition, making it impossible to detect ingestion gaps or measure the full consumption time window.
When I query the Kafka metrics table to build a dashboard showing ingestion health, I can see the most recent timestamp each partition has consumed, but there's no way to know when the oldest unprocessed message in each partition arrived. Without that minimum timestamp, I can't tell whether a partition is genuinely caught up or if there's a gap of stale data behind the latest message.

Log volume counts don't match actual log counts
When I query the log volume buckets table and compare the counts to the actual number of log lines, the numbers are much lower than expected. I assumed each row's count represented the total logs for that service, environment, and severity in the given time window. I didn't realize the stored values are partial counts that must be summed across multiple rows to get a real total.

Five-minute cooldown bypassed after failed recalculation
When a recalculation run fails, I can immediately trigger another one without hitting the rate limit. The five-minute refresh window only applies after a successful run completes — failed runs don't count toward the cooldown at all.

Results disappear after editing experiment settings
After running a metrics recalculation successfully, I edited my experiment's exposure criteria and tried to view the results again — but all the metric results were gone. The run still shows as completed, yet the per-metric results list is empty. I expected the results to persist regardless of later edits to the experiment configuration.

Failed metrics count is inflated when a metric retries
When I look at a completed recalculation run, the failed metrics counter shows 3 even though only one unique metric actually failed — it retried twice before succeeding on the third attempt. Each retry produced its own FAILED result row, and the counter tallies every FAILED row instead of counting distinct failed metrics. I expected the count to reflect how many unique metrics ended in failure, not how many attempts failed.

Scalar CTE with UNION gets wrong type
When I define a scalar CTE using a UNION and then reference it in my query, it resolves without error but the type is wrong — it always resolves as a string regardless of what the subquery actually returns. For example, WITH (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2) AS x, SELECT x + 1 should treat x as an integer, but the resolver assigns it a string type instead. This breaks type-dependent logic downstream.

Expected: the resolver should correctly infer the column type from the first branch of the UNION.

Constant type resolution crashes on unrecognized values
When I pass a numeric constant from a third-party library in my query filter, the type resolver throws an unsupported constant type error and the entire query fails. Standard Python numbers work fine, but values from data processing libraries aren't recognized.

Zero-based array index silently accepted when index is a parameter
When I use a literal zero as an array index, the query builder correctly rejects it with a helpful message about one-based indexing. But when I use a parameter or function call as the index that evaluates to zero, the query passes validation and only fails at runtime with a confusing database error. I expected the same validation regardless of whether the index is a literal or a dynamic expression.

Cohort references in action-level properties are not updated when transferring insights
When I transfer an insight that uses an action with a cohort filter in its properties, the action ID gets rewritten to the new system's ID but the cohort ID inside that action's properties stays pointing to the old system. The insight loads but the cohort filter is broken.

Cohort references in fixed properties of retention queries are not updated during transfer
When I transfer an insight that uses a cohort-based retention query with fixed properties, the cohort ID inside those fixed properties remains pointing to the original account's cohort. After the transfer, the insight breaks because the referenced cohort no longer exists in the destination. I expected all cohort references — including those nested in fixed properties of retention filter entities — to be rewritten to the new account's cohort IDs.

Cohort breakdown transfer fails for single cohort ID
When an insight uses a single cohort ID as a breakdown value (not wrapped in a list), the resource transfer process does not properly include that cohort as a dependency. After migration the insight shows incorrect or missing cohort data because the cohort was not transferred alongside it.

Access token never refreshed when expiry information is lost
When a Google Cloud integration loses its token expiry information, the system treats the access token as still valid and never refreshes it. Batch export jobs then fail with authentication errors once the real token expiration time passes.

Dynamic cohort member list shows duplicates
When I view the members of a dynamic cohort, some people appear more than once in the results. This doesn't happen with static cohorts. I expected each person to appear at most once.

Restoring a session recording playlist sometimes leaves no trace in the activity log
When I restore a deleted playlist from the file system, it reappears but nothing shows up in the activity history — no restored entry like I see for dashboards, insights, or feature flags. This happens intermittently; most restores are logged fine. I expected every restore to be recorded consistently.

Hog function re-enables after restore
When I restore a deleted hog function, it comes back enabled even though I had intentionally disabled it before deleting. I expected the restored function to preserve my disabled setting.

Hog function stays enabled after deletion
When I delete a hog function, it remains enabled in the database instead of being disabled first. I expected the system to automatically disable it as part of the deletion process so that any references wouldn't try to execute it during cleanup.

Person identifier stays stale after a merge
I queried flag evaluations and got the original person identifier instead of the corrected value after merging two people. Unique person counts across evaluations are inflated because merged persons show up multiple times, even though the documentation says merged persons should be counted once.

Session data missing when joining flag evaluations with sessions
When I join flag evaluations with session data, the session fields come back empty even though the evaluation clearly happened during a recorded session. The same join on the events table returns the expected session information. I expected both tables to provide session data the same way.

Wildcard select leaks raw ingestion person ID into results
When I run SELECT * on the flag evaluations table, the raw ingestion-time person ID column shows up in the output alongside the corrected version. I expected the wildcard to hide this internal column since it is only meant as a filtering escape hatch and the corrected person ID is already available.

Session replay metadata undeleted for wrong team after running key restore
I ran the restore command targeting a specific team, but afterward I noticed that session replay events for a different team were also marked as active. The restore only restored keys for one team, yet the ClickHouse metadata update affected sessions across teams. I expected only the sessions belonging to the team I specified to be undeleted.

Restore skips items that already exist with normal state
When running the restore command for a team, some items from the backup are silently skipped. The items already exist in the live table with a normal state, but the restore refuses to overwrite them. I expected the restore to overwrite existing items or at least provide a clearer explanation of why they were skipped.

Command appears frozen while listing recovery points
When I run the restore command without specifying a recovery point, it hangs for several minutes after printing "Listing recovery points in vault" before doing anything else. The vault has many backup snapshots stored, and it seems like the command tries to load all of them before picking one. I expected it to find the latest backup much faster.

Disabled flag reported as active
When I check the status of a feature flag that has been turned off, it still shows as active in the results. I expected a disabled flag to be reported differently since it's no longer being evaluated or served to users.

Release condition without explicit rollout percentage treated as zero instead of defaulting to 100%

I created a release condition without setting a rollout percentage, expecting it to apply to everyone at the default 100%. The status checker treated it as having zero rollout, so my boolean flag showed as partially rolled out and was never flagged as stale, even though it serves one result to everyone.

Boolean flag with no release conditions marked as stale
When I create a new boolean feature flag and leave it without any release conditions, the system treats it as fully rolled out and eventually marks it stale. A completely unconfigured flag should not be considered rolled out to everyone just because no conditions were added.

Region always shows as US
When I run the token generation command for my EU-based team, the output always shows "Region: us" even though my organization is in Europe. I expected it to reflect the correct region so I can paste the right values into the Stripe App dev UI.

Command generates new tokens when existing valid access token is still usable
I ran the token generation command without the force flag, expecting it to reuse my existing valid tokens. Instead it created a completely fresh set. My access token hadn't expired, but the refresh token had been revoked by a cleanup job. I expected the command to detect the still-valid access token and reuse it rather than regenerating everything.

Token generation fails after deleting old OAuth application
After deleting my Stripe OAuth application from the database and running the token generation command again, it failed with an error saying the configured client ID doesn't match any application. I expected the command to detect that the old app was gone and create a new one automatically.

Exposure count stuck at zero for healthy experiments
The experiment dashboard shows zero total exposures even though the experiment has been receiving traffic. The count stays at zero until the next scheduled cycle.

Experiment metrics stuck after a failed recalculation
After a manual recalculation finishes with errors, the next hourly scheduled run is silently skipped and the dashboard still shows old values. It takes up to an hour before fresh data appears again. I expected any new scheduled run to override a stale or broken result rather than being blocked by it.

Admin pagination shows thousands of pages even with few records
When browsing the admin interface, the pagination bar displays an absurdly large number of pages (thousands) even though the table contains only a handful of records. This makes navigation unusable because the page selector is filled with irrelevant page numbers. I expected it to show only the actual number of pages needed for the visible records.

Slot acquisition return value is ambiguous
When trying to acquire a slot for an evaluation check, the function returns None without explaining why. I can't tell if the alert wasn't admitted or if the system is at capacity. The documentation only mentions the capacity case, so I don't know how to recover.

Alert evaluations stop running after extended periods
After my alerts run for several hours, they begin to fail silently and no evaluations execute at all. Restarting the service temporarily fixes the problem, but it always comes back. I expected evaluation slots to be released automatically when each check finishes so that alerts would keep running continuously without manual intervention.

Sync schedule fires at wrong time when sync frequency is shorter than the configured time of day
I set my data sync to run at 3:00 AM with an hourly frequency, but the jobs start running at midnight instead. The scheduled time of day is ignored whenever the sync frequency is shorter than the number of minutes from midnight to the configured time.

Scheduled syncs fire at the wrong time of day
When I configure an external data source to sync at 3 PM, the actual syncs fire at 6 PM instead. The configured sync time is shifted forward and the schedule never runs at the time I set. I expected the sync to honour the exact time I configured.

CDC extraction schedule creation fails when schedule already exists
When I run the CDC extraction schedule setup for a source that already has an active schedule, the operation throws an error instead of updating the existing one. The documentation says it should create or update, so running it a second time should succeed.

Duplicate billing records persist across days despite resends
When a producer corrects a billing record by resending it with updated data, the correction only takes effect if it arrives on the same calendar day as the original. Resends on a different day create a new duplicate entry instead of replacing the old one. I expected every resend of the same record to overwrite the previous version regardless of when it arrived.

Corrected billing quantities persist alongside originals
When a usage producer corrects a previously reported quantity, both the old and new values appear in my billing totals instead of the corrected one replacing the original. I resend the same record with the right amount, but the system keeps the first version I sent.

Migration tool crashes when bridging from legacy migration system
When transitioning from a previous migration system that used its own tracking table, the command crashes with a database error claiming the legacy tracking table doesn't exist, even though the table is present. This happens during the bridge phase when the command tries to check which migrations were already applied by the old system. Instead of crashing, the command should fall back to treating all migrations as new and continuing normally.

Migration refused due to unrelated invalid index
When I try to apply a migration that creates an index concurrently, the command refuses to proceed because it finds an invalid index with the same name in a different schema. The invalid index is from a previous migration in a different schema and has nothing to do with the current migration. I have to manually drop the unrelated index before I can proceed.

Migration doesn't detect broken index from interrupted run
I ran a migration that creates an index concurrently. A previous run was interrupted, leaving an invalid index behind, but the migration didn't catch it and proceeded anyway. Now the query planner sometimes picks the wrong index and performance is degraded. I expected the migration to refuse to run and tell me how to drop the broken index.

Cooldown expires mid-send
When I configure an alert with a cooldown period, two initial notification messages sometimes appear within seconds of each other instead of being properly spaced apart. The first message begins sending but hasn't finished when a second message gets through and posts its own initial notification anyway.

I expected the cooldown setting to reliably prevent any new initial notifications from being delivered for the full duration, no matter how long the first one takes to send.

Root message status gets updated on every reply
When an alert thread has multiple replies, the root message's status line keeps getting rechecked and edited even for non-status events like new errors or comments. I expected only actual status transitions to update the root message, but every single reply triggers a status check that can produce another edit, clutters the thread with redundant updates, and adds unnecessary database lookups on each reply.

Error message shows raw array brackets instead of readable text
When I submit an experiment with invalid settings, the error sometimes displays as square brackets like [] instead of actual text explaining what's wrong. I expected to see a clear description of the configuration problem.

Unexpected technical error shown to users
When an experiment metric calculation fails with an uncommon or unexpected error type, the frontend displays a raw technical exception instead of a friendly message. For example, after a transient database issue, the page showed a low-level stack trace rather than a clear explanation. I expected every failure to produce a readable error message, since this module is supposed to centralize user-friendly error handling for experiments.

Census crashes evaluating teams with no direct scans
The enrollment census crashes when a team has zero direct-scan metric reads in the evaluation window. The crash occurs during the slow read percentage calculation, which divides by the total number of direct reads. This prevents the entire census from completing and blocks enrollment for all teams.

Precompute enrollment undercounts running metrics
When I check the enrollment report, my team shows fewer running metrics than I expect based on all the scheduled metrics I've set up. The enrollment logic only counts scheduled metrics attached to individual experiments, completely missing metrics defined at the team level.

Enrollment doesn't fully roll back on failure
When enrollment fails partway through, the teams already processed stay enrolled instead of being undone. Running the census again adds more teams on top of the partial batch instead of starting fresh.

Command crashes with invalid team ID input
When I run the migration command with --team-ids and accidentally include a non-numeric value like a typo or extra character, the entire command crashes with an unhandled exception instead of showing a helpful error message. I expected the command to validate the comma-separated list and tell me which value is invalid.

Person property values sometimes show unexpected formatting
When viewing person property values in autocomplete suggestions, some entries appear garbled or duplicated. The result formatter tries to parse every value as JSON regardless of type, and when the input isn't a string, the parsing error is silently suppressed and the value is passed through in an incorrect format.

Array property values split into multiple suggestions
When I look up a person or event property that has an array value stored as JSON, each element appears as its own suggestion instead of the full array. For example, if I set a tag property to ["urgent", "review"], the autocomplete shows "urgent" and "review" as separate options rather than showing the combined value as one entry. I expected to see the original array value as a single suggestion.

Deleting an already-removed release returns not found instead of success
When I try to delete a release that no longer exists, the API returns a not found error. I expected the delete operation to succeed silently, since the resource is already gone. This makes it difficult to write idempotent deletion scripts.

Update returns content in no-content response
When I update a release, the response includes a body even though the status is 204 No Content. Some HTTP clients reject responses with bodies on 204 status codes.

Hash id length check says bytes but measures characters
When submitting a hash id containing multi-byte Unicode characters, the system reports that the length cannot exceed 128 bytes, but the actual validation counts characters rather than bytes. A hash with 128 multi-byte characters passes through even though its encoded form exceeds 128 bytes.

Spike event cleanup workflow fails when triggered with an empty input
When I run the spike event cleanup task from the admin interface without specifying any parameters, it crashes with a JSON parsing error instead of running with the default retention period. I expected it to clean up events older than thirty days like it normally does.

Some users don't receive materialization failure notifications even though they have access to the data model
A teammate with full access to our project didn't get a materialization failure alert for a data model they can open in the UI without any issues. Other members with similar access levels received the notification just fine. The model had clearly been failing and needed attention — they simply weren't told. I expected everyone who can access the data model to be notified when it breaks.

Schema selection ignores later modifier changes
After changing query modifiers mid-query, the events schema still reflects the original configuration instead of the updated one. I expected that modifying the modifiers would take effect on subsequent calls within the same context.

Resource reference tags return null instead of empty arrays
When a query doesn't reference any saved queries, warehouse tables, or direct reads, the resource tags come back as null instead of empty arrays. Downstream tools that expect arrays and try to iterate over the values will crash.

Sensitive values can overwrite regular values in query parameters
When building a query that needs both regular and sensitive parameter values, the wrong value sometimes gets substituted during execution. This happens intermittently — if I add a regular value first, then a sensitive one, then another regular value, the third value ends up replacing the sensitive one in the final query. The result is that the query returns incorrect data or exposes sensitive information under a non-sensitive placeholder.

Expected behavior: each parameter value gets a unique placeholder regardless of whether it was added via the regular or sensitive path.

Symbol set never gets linked to its release after bulk upload
I uploaded symbol sets for a new release, but when I check the dashboard the symbol sets show up without any release association. The upload completes successfully and the source maps are there, yet the release binding step appears to have been skipped. If I re-upload the same chunks with the release ID included, they still don't get linked. I expected the bulk upload process to associate existing orphaned symbol sets with the release they were shipped in.

Symbol sets are being deleted while still actively deployed
I upload a new release with unchanged source maps, but after some time the symbol sets disappear from the UI and exceptions can no longer be symbolicated. The chunks haven't changed between deploys, so the rows should persist indefinitely. They get removed as if they were abandoned, even though they're still in active use across multiple releases.

Array contains filter returns false positives
When I filter activity logs by an array field using the contains operation, the results include records where the search term appears as a substring anywhere in the JSON detail field, not just inside the specified array. For example, searching for a change type like "button" also matches records where "button" appears as part of another word or in a completely different field. I expected the filter to only match when the value actually exists as an element in the target array.

Exact filter on array field returns partial matches
When I filter activity logs for an exact value in a simple array field like changes[], entries containing a substring of my search value are returned instead of only exact matches. For example, searching for "update" also returns entries where the array contains "updated". I expected exact matching to return only items that match the full value precisely.

Issue description changes don't appear in activity history
When I edit an issue's description and save it, the change doesn't show up in the activity history. Other fields like status and name are recorded correctly, but description edits are invisible in the audit trail even though the new text is saved.

Splitting an issue sometimes leaves no trace in the activity log
When I split an issue, it divides correctly but the action doesn't show up in my team's activity history. Other mutations like merging or updating always appear there. This makes it hard to audit who split what and when.

Assignment email sent even when assignment fails to save
When I assign an issue to someone, the assigned person sometimes receives an email notification but the assignment doesn't actually stick — reloading the page shows no assignee. This seems to happen intermittently, suggesting a race condition.

Expected: the email should only be sent if the assignment is successfully saved.

Workflow silently uses team ID 0 when no input is given
When I trigger the daily intent clustering without specifying any parameters, it completes successfully but returns results for team ID 0 instead of failing or prompting for a team. I expected either an error asking me to specify a team or at least a warning in the logs.

Skipped reports sometimes lack an explanation
When a count-triggered evaluation wasn't triggered because the result count hadn't reached the threshold yet, the response showed the report as not due but gave no reason. Monitoring couldn't distinguish between reports skipped due to cooldowns or daily caps and those simply waiting for more data.

Report says completed but has no sections or metrics

It looks like a blank report that was labeled as done. I expected either actual findings in the report or a clear indication that nothing could be generated rather than a completed status with empty content.

Report prompt guidance always empty
When I configure an evaluation with custom prompt guidance, the guidance doesn't appear in the generated report context. It comes through blank every time regardless of what I set. I expected my guidance text to be included so the agent knows how to structure the report.

Backfill progress counter freezes midway through evaluation window

I expected the progress to continue until all eligible units were evaluated.

Duplicate evaluations fire during reruns

Backfill settle window extends beyond configured value

Async query status endpoint returns 400 for internal server errors

Query log endpoint returns nothing for queries run today

Queries from previous days show up fine. I expected to be able to look up the log for any recent query regardless of whether it was run today or yesterday.

Async auth check always succeeds regardless of credentials

Page crashes when integration lookup fails for non-budget reasons

I expected the page to always show ownership information, with anonymous read as a fallback.

Sluggish performance after a force push persists for hours

I expected the performance to recover within minutes once the repository was back to a normal state.

Deletion verification never marks records as confirmed

Deletion process stops after first batch failure

Bulk data deletion only removes the last item

Plugin server health metrics show misspelled names

Person/session data merge fails for records with certain Unicode characters

Missing baseline comparison in spike alerts

Spiking alert omits event count

Alert headline disappears after editing

Steps funnel with breakdown shows only one series per step instead of one per breakdown value

Single-step funnel with conversion from previous saves but fails at evaluation

Conversion rate drops spuriously when only one period of data exists

Lag feature function returns wrong array shape when no lags are requested

Sample percent produces biased results

I expected the sample to be more representative of the full alert population.

S3 offload silently drops uploads under burst traffic

Web vitals path breakdown shows inflated values after re-running precomputation

Web vitals queries become very slow over time
As more data accumulates, queries for web vitals metrics take progressively longer to complete. Some backend nodes handle most of the data while others stay nearly empty, causing uneven load and degraded performance for dashboard loading.

Scoring summary counts include results from failed partition batches
After running the session replay scoring workflow, the final tally shows more sessions scored than expected. Some partition batches failed during processing, but their partial results were still added to the overall count. I expected the summary to only reflect sessions from batches that completed successfully.

Scored session count exceeds fetched count
When I check the results of the scoring job, the number of scored sessions is sometimes higher than the number of fetched sessions for the same chunk. This doesn't make sense since we should only be able to score what we've fetched. I expected scored to never exceed fetched.

Funnel alert evaluates incomplete data buckets
I set up a funnel alert with a minimum threshold and a fast check schedule, but it keeps triggering on data that hasn't fully accumulated yet. When I tried the same pattern with a trend alert, the system refused to save it unless I added a maximum threshold. I expected funnel alerts to have the same protection against evaluating partial time periods.

Notebook widget save fails even with valid inputs
I configured a notebook widget by selecting both the source notebook and a widget snapshot, but the save fails with an error telling me to provide both fields. I verified that both fields contain valid values, so the rejection seems incorrect.

Role assignee filter rejects valid short identifiers
When I try to filter recent tickets by a role assignee, the request fails saying the role identifier must be a UUID. I'm using the short code shown in the role settings, which is how all other role references work in the product.

Priority filter gives no details on invalid values
When I filter conversation tickets by priority and include an invalid priority, the API returns a generic error without telling me which priorities are invalid. I have to guess which of my selected priorities is wrong instead of getting a clear list of rejected values.

Pre-aggregated web vitals table ignores query context
When querying the pre-aggregated web vitals table through HogQL, the underlying ClickHouse table selection does not respect the query context. I noticed that passing different query settings or contexts has no effect on which table is used — the same distributed table is always returned regardless of context. I expected the context to allow selecting between different table variants (for example, a local vs. distributed table depending on the query settings).

Usage metric timestamps are always in UTC
The timestamps on my usage metrics appear to be in UTC even though my team is set to a different timezone. I expected the timestamps to reflect my team's local timezone.
